title: Boundary-condition independence of infinite-chain ground states in the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain
abstract: Extending the analytic machinery and using the numerical inputs from OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we study infinite-chain ground states of the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic model $H=\sum_j\{\boldsymbol S_j\cdot\boldsymbol S_{j+1}+D(S_j^{\mathrm z})^2\}$ for sufficiently small $|D|$. We consider two finite-volume settings: periodic chains with an even number of sites, and open chains with an odd number of sites and the same positive magnetic field in the $\mathrm z$ direction at both endpoints. We prove that the ground states in each setting have an infinite-chain limit along the full sequence, without passing to a subsequence, and that the two limiting states coincide. Convergence is uniform in $D$ on a fixed neighborhood of zero. The common limit is a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, and its local expectation values depend continuously on $D$. These conclusions concern the two specified constructions, not uniqueness among all infinite-chain ground states. They provide the input for the study of a topological phase transition in a forthcoming revision of our companion paper.   The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the inductive estimates and to completing the proof.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes that the ground state of the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain is independent of the boundary conditions (periodic vs. open) in the thermodynamic limit. By comparing finite-volume calculations, the authors prove the existence of a unique, gapped, and continuous limiting state $\omega_D$. This result is crucial for understanding the bulk properties of this quantum magnetic material.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the boundary-condition independence of the infinite-chain ground state for the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic model.
main_result: It proves that the ground states derived from periodic and open-chain boundary conditions converge to the same, symmetric, locally-unique gapped infinite-chain limit state, $\omega_D$.
method: The proof involves comparing the ground state expectation values derived from two different finite-volume constructions (periodic vs. open/field) and taking the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The system is the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain described by the Hamiltonian $H=\sum_j\{ oldsymbol S_j\cdot oldsymbol S_{j+1}+D(S_z^2)_j\}$. The analysis uses finite-volume approximations for both periodic and open boundary conditions.
